identity.what_it_is: A private, shareholder-owned beach club in Newport, Rhode Island, open to public day-use via parking/season passes since 1952
identity.where: Newport, Rhode Island, USA, on Ocean Drive/Ocean Avenue between Bailey's Beach and Hazard's Beach
identity.warnings: Not the same place as Gooseberry Island (Westport, Massachusetts), an unrelated island whose homes were destroyed by Hurricane Carol in 1954 - do not mix that island's storm/state-park history into this beach's copy. Address conflict: gooseberrybeach.com gives 130 Ocean Avenue; VisitRhodeIsland gives 123 Ocean Drive. No harvested source supports a 'Hazard Avenue' access route or names Newport State Airport (NPT) or T.F. Green (PVD) in connection with this beach; that reconciliation is not sourced here.

spike_candidates.statement: A shareholder beach club since 1952 charges $30-$40/day and bans walk-ons, yet in 2021 faced a lawsuit threat demanding free resident access under its own founding deed.
spike_candidates.tension: It brands itself a steward welcoming the public while paying a police officer to block rideshare drop-offs and fighting a resident's claim that it violates the very 1952 deed it cites as proof of openness.

spike_candidates.statement: RIDOH closed Gooseberry to swimming for bacteria in June 2022 and again in August 2025, with 2022 testing finding unsafe bacteria on nearly half the days sampled.
spike_candidates.tension: A beach charging premium parking fees for 'calm, clear waters' is repeatedly too contaminated to legally swim in, just two summers apart.

facts.fact: Gooseberry Beach is a private beach in Newport, Rhode Island, off Ocean Drive, that is also open to the public.
facts.quote: gooseberry beach is a beach located in newport, rhode island off ocean drive . it is a private beach, but also open to the public.
facts.source_title: Gooseberry Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: A separate, unrelated Gooseberry Island in Westport, Massachusetts lost most of its houses when Hurricane Carol hit in 1954 and has been uninhabited since.
facts.quote: the island used to have many residents, especially during the summer months, until hurricane carol destroyed most homes on the island in 1954.
facts.source_title: Gooseberry Island (Massachusetts) - Wikipedia

facts.fact: News coverage in 2025 again distinguishes the two neighboring properties: Bailey's Beach is a private member-owned club, while Gooseberry Beach is a private beach that is also open to the public.
facts.quote: bailey's beach is a private member-owned club, while gooseberry beach is a private beach that is also open to the public.
facts.source_title: Two Newport beaches closed due to high bacteria levels - What's Up Newp

facts.fact: Gooseberry sits in a cove protected by a spit of land and large boulders roughly 75 meters offshore at high tide and no more than 50 meters at low tide.
facts.quote: gooseberry itself is nestled in a sort of cove, protected by a spit of land and several large boulders roughly 75 metres offshore at high tide, no more than 50 at low tide.
facts.source_title: Gooseberry Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: The beach lies between Bailey's Beach and Hazard's Beach on Newport's Ocean Drive.
facts.quote: the beach is located between bailey's beach and hazard's beach.
facts.source_title: Gooseberry Beach - Wikipedia

facts.fact: Gooseberry Beach is catalogued at 41°27'35.0"N 71°19'12.1"W with GNIS Feature ID 1219462 and OpenStreetMap node 357257785.
facts.quote: gnis feature id 1219462 0 references openstreetmap node id 357257785 0 references
facts.source_title: Gooseberry Beach (Q5584121) - Wikidata

facts.fact: The land that became Gooseberry Beach was mid-19th-century farmland called Rocky Farm, owned by John Alfred Hazard, a descendant of one of Newport's founders.
facts.quote: in the mid-19th century this property was called rocky farm and was owned by one man, john alfred hazard, a descendant of one of newport's founders.
facts.source_title: John Alfred Hazard's Newport Legacy - Hazard's Beach, Gooseberry Beach, and Gooseberry Island

facts.fact: John Alfred Hazard died in 1880 and his will became the subject of contention and controversy.
facts.quote: upon his death in 1880, his will was the subject of contention and controversy.
facts.source_title: John Alfred Hazard's Newport Legacy - Hazard's Beach, Gooseberry Beach, and Gooseberry Island

facts.fact: The contested Hazard estate resulted in Rocky Farm being gifted to Newport Hospital, an organization unprepared to manage it.
facts.quote: it resulted in the gift of rocky farm to the newport hospital, an organization entirely unprepared for its management.
facts.source_title: John Alfred Hazard's Newport Legacy - Hazard's Beach, Gooseberry Beach, and Gooseberry Island

facts.fact: Two separate beaches, Hazard's Beach and Gooseberry Beach, eventually resulted from the Rocky Farm land, each owned and run by corporations formed by local citizens.
facts.quote: two separate beaches- hazard's beach and gooseberry beach-eventually resulted, each owned and run by corporations formed by local citizens.
facts.source_title: John Alfred Hazard's Newport Legacy - Hazard's Beach, Gooseberry Beach, and Gooseberry Island

facts.fact: Hazard's donation was central to the development of a major portion of Ocean Drive from the late 1880s until the mid-1950s.
facts.quote: john alfred hazard's donation was central to the development of a major portion of the ocean drive from the late 1880s until the mid-1950s.
facts.source_title: John Alfred Hazard's Newport Legacy - Hazard's Beach, Gooseberry Beach, and Gooseberry Island

facts.fact: Gooseberry Beach's shareholders have operated the beach as stewards of the property since 1952, per the beach's own president.
facts.quote: since 1952, the shareholders of gooseberry beach have prided themselves on serving as stewards of this beautiful natural resource while welcoming generations of newport families and beyond to enjoy the beach and facilities
facts.source_title: Part-time resident threatens legal action against Gooseberry and Hazard's Beaches over public access - Newport Buzz

facts.fact: Gooseberry's president says the club provides even more public access than its 1952 deed with Newport Hospital requires.
facts.quote: since 1952, the shareholders of gooseberry beach have prided themselves on serving as stewards of this beautiful natural resource while welcoming generations of newport families and beyond to enjoy the beach and facilities
facts.source_title: Gooseberry ensures public beach access - Newport This Week

facts.fact: George Loftus is president of Gooseberry Beach, Inc. and is the entity's public-facing spokesperson in disputes over beach access.
facts.quote: gooseberry beach president george loftus responded to her claims in a communication with newport city manager joe nicholson
facts.source_title: Part-time resident threatens legal action against Gooseberry and Hazard's Beaches over public access - Newport Buzz

facts.fact: Gooseberry Beach does not permit drop-offs or walk-on entry; access is by vehicle, bike, or scooter with a paid pass only.
facts.quote: drop offs/walk-ons are not permitted.
facts.source_title: Guest Parking | Gooseberry Beach

facts.fact: Gooseberry Beach's own site lists its address as 130 Ocean Avenue, Newport, RI.
facts.quote: 130 ocean avenue, newport, ri
facts.source_title: Guest Parking | Gooseberry Beach

facts.fact: The beach is open daily 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. (weather permitting) with lifeguards on duty the same hours.
facts.quote: open daily 9 am - 5 pm lifeguards on duty 9 am - 5 pm
facts.source_title: Guest Parking | Gooseberry Beach

facts.fact: Weekday non-member car parking costs $30 (plus 7% RI sales tax and fees), capped at 5 people per vehicle.
facts.quote: daily parking is $30 per car (plus fees) not exceeding 5 people per vehicle.
facts.source_title: Guest Parking | Gooseberry Beach

facts.fact: Weekend and holiday non-member car parking costs $40 plus 7% RI sales tax.
facts.quote: weekend/holiday non-member parking rate $40 ( plus 7% ri sales tax)
facts.source_title: Guest Parking | Gooseberry Beach

facts.fact: Effective June 29, 2026, Gooseberry's parking lot went cashless, accepting only credit or debit cards.
facts.quote: effective june 29, 2026, the parking lot is cashless.
facts.source_title: Guest Parking | Gooseberry Beach

facts.fact: Bikes, e-bikes, and scooters pay a $10 daily parking fee, with a season bike pass priced at $100.
facts.quote: bikes, e-bikes, scooters $10
facts.source_title: Guest Parking | Gooseberry Beach

facts.fact: Gooseberry Beach bans alcohol, pets, grilling, motorized watercraft, open fires, spearfishing, and tents, though small infant tents are allowed.
facts.quote: the following are prohibited: alcohol, pets, grilling, motorized watercrafts, open fires, spearfishing and tents (small infant tents are allowed).
facts.source_title: Guest Parking | Gooseberry Beach

facts.fact: The beach's only food vendor is a cash-only 'snack shack' open 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., weather permitting.
facts.quote: " snack shack " is open 11 am - 5 pm ( weather permitting ) - cash only
facts.source_title: Guest Parking | Gooseberry Beach

facts.fact: Gooseberry Beach's homepage carries the tagline 'we rock.'
facts.quote: gooseberry beach | we "rock"
facts.source_title: Gooseberry Beach | We "Rock"

facts.fact: Beyond shareholder access, Gooseberry issues seasonal parking passes to non-shareholders and offers daily passes to the public depending on beach capacity.
facts.quote: gooseberry beach issues seasonal parking passes for non-shareholders. it also makes daily passes available to the public, depending on beach capacity.
facts.source_title: Part-time resident threatens legal action against Gooseberry and Hazard's Beaches over public access - Newport Buzz

facts.fact: In June 2021, part-time Newport/Miami resident Brooke Richter retained attorney Amy Rice to pursue legal action seeking to make Gooseberry essentially a public beach for Newport residents.
facts.quote: brooke richter, 55, of miami, florida and newport, ri, has retained middletown attorney amy rice to represent her in a quest to make gooseberry essentially a public beach for newport residents.
facts.source_title: Part-time resident threatens legal action against Gooseberry and Hazard's Beaches over public access - Newport Buzz

facts.fact: Rising rideshare drop-offs and pick-ups on narrow, shoulderless Ocean Drive got dangerous enough that Gooseberry had to hire a police officer to direct traffic.
facts.quote: gooseberry had to employ a police officer to help direct traffic.
facts.source_title: Part-time resident threatens legal action against Gooseberry and Hazard's Beaches over public access - Newport Buzz

facts.fact: On June 8, 2022, RIDOH recommended closing Gooseberry Beach to swimming due to high bacteria levels, the first beach closure notification of that year.
facts.quote: the rhode island department of health (ridoh) recommends closing gooseberry beach in newport for swimming because of high bacteria levels. this is the first beach closure notification of the year from ridoh.
facts.source_title: RIDOH recommends closing Gooseberry Beach in Newport for swimming - GoLocalProv

facts.fact: On June 27, 2026, RIDOH recommended re-opening the swimming areas at Hazard's and Gooseberry Beach after bacteria counts returned to safe levels.
facts.quote: the rhode island department of health (ridoh) recommends re-opening the swimming areas at hazards and gooseberry beach in newport because bacteria counts have returned to safe levels.
facts.source_title: RIDOH recommends re-opening the swimming areas at Hazards and Gooseberry Beach

facts.fact: On August 14, 2025, RIDOH recommended closing swimming areas at two Newport beaches, Bailey's/Spouting Rock and Gooseberry, due to high bacteria counts.
facts.quote: the rhode island department of health has recommended closing swimming areas at two newport beaches due to high bacteria counts, officials announced thursday.
facts.source_title: Two Newport beaches closed due to high bacteria levels - What's Up Newp

facts.fact: Spouting Rock and Gooseberry beaches reopened just two days after their August 2025 closure once bacteria levels dropped back to safe ranges, while Easton's Beach stayed closed.
facts.quote: the quick reopening of spouting rock and gooseberry beaches shows how rapidly water quality can change during summer months. both locations were closed for just two days before bacteria levels dropped back to safe ranges.
facts.source_title: Two Newport beaches reopen as Easton's Beach remains closed - What's Up Newp

facts.fact: RI beach closures are triggered when saltwater samples exceed 60 colony-forming units of bacteria per 100 milliliters.
facts.quote: bacteria levels are measured in colony forming units per 100 milliliters, with closures triggered when saltwater samples exceed 60 cfu/100ml.
facts.source_title: Two Newport beaches reopen as Easton's Beach remains closed - What's Up Newp

facts.fact: A 2023 water-quality report found Gooseberry Beach had high bacteria levels on nearly half the days it was tested in 2022, one of 14 Rhode Island beaches exceeding the safety threshold on 25% or more of tested days.
facts.quote: in rhode island, 14 beaches exceeded this safety threshold on 25% or more of the days tested last year, with gooseberry beach in newport having high bacteria levels on nearly half of the days it was tested.
facts.source_title: Report: Pathogens Pose Public Health Risk at Southern New England Beaches - ecoRI News

facts.fact: Gooseberry sits in a cove that produces calmer waves and a more family-friendly swimming experience than open-water Newport beaches.
facts.quote: gooseberry beach is located along ocean avenue in newport. it is situated in a cove making for calmer waves and a more family-friendly swimming experience.
facts.source_title: Gooseberry Beach - Swim Guide

facts.fact: As a Tier II beach, Gooseberry is water-quality sampled monthly, from around May 26 through September 1 each season.
facts.quote: gooseberry beach is sampled monthly from may 26th to september 1st.
facts.source_title: Gooseberry Beach - Swim Guide

facts.fact: Rhode Island's constitution guarantees the public the right to fishery and shore privileges under the state's charter and usages.
facts.quote: the public shall continue to enjoy and freely exercise all the rights of fishery, and the privileges of the shore, to which they have been heretofore entitled under the charter and usages of this state.
facts.source_title: State of the Beach/State Reports/RI/Beach Access - Beachapedia

facts.fact: Rhode Island is the only U.S. state to specifically enumerate four shoreline rights in its constitution: fishing, gathering seaweed, swimming access via the shore, and passage along the sea.
facts.quote: rhode island is the only state to specifically outline four shoreline rights -- fishing, gathering seaweed, swimming access via the shore and passage along the sea.
facts.source_title: State of the Beach/State Reports/RI/Beach Access - Beachapedia

facts.fact: A Rhode Island tourism listing gives Gooseberry Beach's address as 123 Ocean Drive, Newport, RI 02840, conflicting with the beach's own listed address.
facts.quote: gooseberry beach 123 ocean drive, newport, ri 02840 newport county
facts.source_title: Gooseberry Beach | Newport, RI 02840 - Visit Rhode Island

facts.fact: A tourism listing describes Gooseberry as a scenic cove beach known for calm, clear waters, white sand, and views of large estates, with a cafe, restrooms, and a roughly $30 daily vehicle-entrance fee, and walk-ons restricted.
facts.quote: gooseberry beach is a popular, scenic cove beach in newport, rhode island, known for its calm, clear waters, white sand, and views of large estates, offering amenities like a cafe and restrooms but requiring a per-vehicle entrance fee for parking, though walk-ons are restricted.
facts.source_title: Gooseberry Beach | Newport, RI 02840 - Visit Rhode Island
